author: blu
body: An unblocked attacker deals its power to the defending player -- unless that player controls a Circle of Protection for the attacker's colour, which prevents the damage (dmg 0). Lifelink gains only what is actually dealt, so a prevented hit gains nothing. (Trample excess and non-combat burn are gated elsewhere; trample-excess CoP is a documented gap -- trample-over lacks the attacker's colour without a signature change.)

author: blu
body: trample-over deals a trampling attacker's excess (power beyond the total lethal its blockers absorb) to the defending player. Excess is read from the pre-damage battlefield (pre), because the lethal each blocker needs is its toughness minus damage it already had -- reading it after assign-damage-to-blockers would double-count the trample assignment and trample the full power. A non-trample attacker, or one whose power did not exceed its blockers' toughness, changes nothing.

author: blu
body: Deathtouch: any nonzero combat damage from a deathtouch source is lethal. Rather than destroy mid-combat (which would leave the damage loops finding a removed permanent), a deathtouch hit marks the target with overwhelming damage, so the ordinary post-combat state-based-action sweep (sba-lethal-loop) destroys it -- and a regeneration shield still saves it, exactly as the rules intend. Non-deathtouch damage is unchanged, so all existing combat behaves identically.
